estimatedFields: the times at the three waypoints and the go/no-go hold (no flown times found; the scene spaces them before the capture as the pre-launch plan on Everyday Astronaut did: WP0 76 min, WP1 51 min, WP2 10 min before capture, the hold ending 4 min before)
the burn, capture and hard-capture times to the minute only (the NASA blog and AmericaSpace give hh:mm EDT); the burn's length is AmericaSpace's 'roughly 90 seconds'

Waypoints 1 and 2 on the docking axis ahead of the port (AmericaSpace gives their ranges, not their direction; not to be confused with the 220 m Wikipedia gives as the limit of Hurley's touchscreen flying); Waypoint 0 400 m below the station
the closing speed and the path between the waypoints (no flown figures found)

the nose cone's side and opening angle (the Everyday Astronaut Demo-2 timeline has its opening sequence start at T+00:12:48, 46 s after separation, without saying whether planned or flown: the scene shows it open throughout)

the docking system under the nose cone and the station away from the port end (the ISS is the /iss diagram model as of 31 May 2020, scaled to metres, with its own Soyuz and Progress models on their sourced ports and Pirs drawn at the diagram's size; only Harmony's forward end, PMA-2, IDA-2 and HTV-9 are drawn to their sourced sizes)
the ring's retraction between soft and hard capture (its travel)

provenance.l: NASA Space Station blog, 31 May 2020: Crew Dragon docked at 10:16 a.m. EDT (soft capture) over the border of northern China and Mongolia, 262 miles above the Earth; hard capture at 10:27 a.m. EDT, 12 hooks closed

AmericaSpace, 31 May 2020: the roughly 90-second Approach Initiation burn at 8:11 a.m. EDT into the ISS Approach Ellipsoid; Waypoint Zero 1,300 ft (400 m) below the station, Waypoint One 720 ft (220 m), Waypoint Two 66 ft (20 m) with a go/no-go poll; Hurley took manual control a second time in close proximity; contact and capture with IDA-2 at the forward end of Harmony at 10:16 a.m. EDT
NASA Space Station blog, 25 May 2020: HTV-9 installed on Harmony's Earth-facing port
Harmony: 6.7 m long, 4.4 m across (Wikipedia, Harmony (ISS module))

Pressurized Mating Adapter: 1.86 m (6.1 ft) long, 1.9 m (6.25 ft) at the wide end, 1.37 m (4.5 ft) at the narrow end (NASA, International Space Station elements reference, mirrored by the National Space Society)
International Docking Adapter: 110 cm high, 160 cm wide (about 240 cm with the targets); IDA-2 on PMA-2 since 19 Aug 2016 (Wikipedia)
HTV: 9.8 m long including the main thruster, 4.4 m across (JAXA)

PMA-2 moved with Harmony to Harmony's final location, its forward port, in November 2007 (Canadarm2 put PMA-2 on Harmony's forward port on 12 Nov 2007; the pair moved two days later) (Wikipedia, Pressurized Mating Adapter)

Everyday Astronaut, Demo-2 timeline: Dragon separates from the second stage at T+00:12:02, the nosecone opening sequence starts at T+00:12:48; the pre-launch planned times of the waypoints and capture
NASA Space Station blog, 25 Apr 2020: Progress 75 docked to the Zvezda service module; Progress 74, Progress 75 and Soyuz MS-16 attached to the station
Soyuz MS-16 docked at Poisk's zenith port on 9 April 2020 (Wikipedia, Soyuz MS-16)
Progress MS-13 (74P) docked at Pirs on 9 December 2019 and left in July 2020 (Wikipedia, Progress MS-13)
